Answer: F
Reason: The chest X-ray of the 12-year-old patient (Figure 1) displays marked reticulonodular opacities and cystic changes predominantly in the upper lobes, indicative of advanced interstitial lung disease, whereas the 3-year-old patient's X-ray (Figure 4) shows relatively clear lung fields with minimal to no such upper lobe pathology. This demonstrates that the subpleural lung cysts and associated interstitial changes are significantly more prominent in the older patient.
